messages:
Alex H: Hey team — Acme (trial) is hitting 429s during a sponsored hackathon load test since ~10:02 PT. Saw a flurry of small chat requests, then constant 429s. Can someone quick-check headers/limits?
Meera R: @Alex H can you paste one of the raw responses or the request-id + headers? 429 body and any Retry-After helps.
Alex H: Paste below: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1719504340
retry-after: 12
{ "error": { "message": "Rate limit exceeded" }, "request_id": "req_0472a9" }
```
We were spinning 80 parallel requests from the demo script (node). Org: org-acme-9. Key: redacted.
Tyler W: 80 parallel on free tier will hit concurrency caps. Free plan usually has burst but limited sustained throughput. Did they use streaming? That many concurrent sessions also spikes token throughput.
Alex H: They were doing short non-streamed chat completions, ~200 tokens each. Hackathon workload: ~25 reqs/sec sustained for ~3m, then peaks.
Meera R: OK repro sounds clear. Two buckets: per-second token throughput + per-connection concurrency. Free accounts: soft concurrency ~20 and per-minute token budget that will exhaust with that pattern. The headers show remaining=0 and retry-after=12 -> token-based throttle triggered.
Meera R: Quick mitigations: reduce parallelism (<=20), add exponential backoff on 429, or shard test keys across org if this is internal load test. Longer term: upgrade to paid or request a temporary burst uplift.
Alex H: Customer asks if we can do a temporary exception for the 3-4 hour hackathon window. They're not yet on paid plan. Is that possible?
Sales Ops: @Alex H we can enable a short-term uplift as a sales-assisted exception for non-paying accounts for events like hackathons. Need customer billing contact + expected peak TPS and window. We'll require a handshake with billing to enable a temporary cap increase.
Alex H: Contact is jamie@acme.com. Expected peak 60 reqs/sec for ~4 hours, ~200 tokens/req.
Meera R: I'll draft a repro & safe-fallback guidance for them so we don't accidentally burn infra: include backoff, ephemeral token rotation, and check X-RateLimit-Remaining header before heavy loops. Example snippet: 
```
for (const id of jobs) {
  const r = await fetch(url, opts);
  if (r.status === 429) {
    await sleep(parseInt(r.headers.get('retry-after') || '10') * 1000);
    // exponential backoff
  }
}
```
ops-bot: Support ticket created #SUP-2026-788 (auto)
Sales Ops: Created a 24-hour temporary uplift for org-acme-9 until 1719580800. Noted billing contact, sent confirmation to jamie@acme.com. If they expect recurring hackathons, we should propose a paid reserved capacity trial.
Tyler W: For immediate dev guidance: suggest non-streamed batching (combine prompts where possible), lower concurrency, and prefer smaller max_tokens to keep token-rate low. Also validate they aren't reusing the same API key from multiple testers — key sharing can make it look like a single client with massive concurrency.
Alex H: Sharing this to Acme now. Any internal followups?
Meera R: Action items: (1) Confirm uplift window and start time with Sales Ops (done), (2) Send short doc to customer with repro & backoff snippet, (3) Monitor metrics for org-acme-9 during event — I'll watch error and latency dashboards.
Sales Ops: I'll follow up post-event for conversion. Added sales owner tag. :tada:
Alex H: Thanks all :raised_hands: — will close thread after the hackathon.
Meera R: Marking note: recommended long-term path = paid Reserved/Dedicated or trial of Dedicated burst for predictable throughput.
Alex H: Closing loop — Acme confirmed receipt and will throttle clients. They said uplift helped.
Meera R: Closing ticket SUP-2026-788 and adding internal postmortem note to support case: cause = free-tier concurrency + token throughput spike; remediation = temporary uplift + client-side backoff + upgrade convo.
